anomalies.observed: On the AVR-ISP-6 programming header J7 the pin numbers and function names are swapped relative to the standard 6-pin AVR ISP pinout: pin 5 is labelled 'SCK' and carries NET0007, while pin 3 is labelled 'RST' and carries NET0006. Tracing the nets shows NET0007 also lands on the MCU SCK pin (U4.7 / U1.7 = PB2/SCK) and NET0006 on the MCU RESET pin (U4.1 / U1.1 = PB5/RESET), so the MCU-side mapping is correct but the connector pads are reversed.
anomalies.expected: The standard AVR-ISP-6 (2x3) pinout is pin 1=MISO, pin 2=VCC, pin 3=SCK, pin 4=MOSI, pin 5=RESET, pin 6=GND. Therefore SCK (NET0007) should be on J7 pin 3 and RESET (NET0006) on J7 pin 5.

evidence.quote: J7 'AVR-ISP-6': pin1 MISO->NET0010, pin4 MOSI->NET0003, pin5 SCK->NET0007, pin3 RST->NET0006 (sheet /, page 1, area C4)
U4 pin7 XTAL1/PB3... pin7 PB2 -> NET0007; pin1 RESET/PB5 -> NET0006 (page 2, area B)

anomalies.impact: A standard AVR ISP programmer cable plugged into J7 will swap the SCK and RESET lines: the programmer's clock will be driven onto the MCU reset pin and the programmer's reset onto the SCK pin, so the device cannot be programmed or debugged over the header (and the MCU may be held in reset during programming attempts).

parsed.summary: The fan-controller build is largely coherent, but the AVR-ISP-6 programming header J7 has its SCK and RESET pins transposed (SCK on pad 5, RST on pad 3) versus the universal 2x3 ISP pinout, which would break in-circuit programming with a standard programmer.
